blocks.text: Where to Find 55+ Rancher and Master-on-Main Townhomes in Abbotsford

parts.t: Abbotsford is one of the Fraser Valley's most established downsizer markets because of its deep selection of 55+ age-restricted townhome communities built on flat, walkable land around Mill Lake Park, Clearbrook, and McMillan. Unlike newer three-storey family townhomes built with steep stairs and tandem garages, Abbotsford's 55+ adult townhome complexes were designed specifically for single-level living—featuring wide floor plans (1,300 to 2,400+ sq ft), main-floor primary bedrooms with walk-in showers, private patios, and double side-by-side garages with full driveways.

Buyers comparing 55+ townhomes in Abbotsford generally choose between two layouts: (1) true single-level rancher townhomes on a crawlspace or slab in Central Abbotsford (Gladwin Road, Ware Street, and Marshall Road) and Clearbrook, offering zero interior stairs; and (2) rancher-with-basement or master-on-main townhomes in East Abbotsford (McMillan, Old Clayburn, and Ledgeview/Whatcom) and West Abbotsford, which keep all daily living on the main floor while providing a full lower level or upper loft for visiting family, hobbies, and storage.

blocks.text: How BC's 55+ Age Restriction Rules Work in Strata Townhomes

parts.t: Under British Columbia's Strata Property Act (Bill 44 amendments), 55+ is the only age restriction that strata corporations are legally permitted to enforce (all former 19+, 35+, and 45+ bylaws were automatically converted unless they met the 55+ threshold or were updated to 55+). In a valid 55+ Abbotsford townhome complex, at least one resident occupying the home must be 55 years of age or older, while a younger spouse or partner, live-in caregivers, and certain exempted occupants are permitted under provincial regulations. Before offering, always review the strata bylaws for exact occupancy wording, pet rules, workshop/clubhouse amenities, and roof/envelope history in the Depreciation Report.

blocks.text: 7 Common Questions About Abbotsford 55+ Townhomes for Sale

parts.t: How does the 55+ age rule work when buying an Abbotsford adult townhome?

Under BC's Strata Property Act, a 55+ age-restricted strata bylaw requires that at least one person residing in the unit be 55 or older. A younger spouse or partner is permitted to live with the 55+ resident, and an investor under 55 may own the unit provided any tenant occupying it meets the 55+ requirement.
What happened to 45+ and 19+ townhome complexes in Abbotsford?

When BC amended the Strata Property Act in November 2022, all age restrictions below 55+ (such as 19+, 40+, and 45+) became unenforceable. Some formerly 45+ Abbotsford complexes subsequently voted to adopt a 55+ bylaw, while others now operate as all-ages communities.
Where are most 55+ rancher townhomes located in Abbotsford?

Most 55+ rancher and master-on-main townhome communities sit in Central Abbotsford (near Mill Lake Park, Gladwin Road, and Marshall Road), Clearbrook in Abbotsford West, and McMillan / Old Clayburn in Abbotsford East.
Do Abbotsford 55+ townhomes have double side-by-side garages?

Yes, a major advantage of Abbotsford's established 55+ rancher townhomes is that most offer either a full double side-by-side garage or a single garage plus an adjacent driveway spot, along with clubhouses, RV parking in select complexes, and guest suites.
Can I bring a dog or cat into a 55+ townhome in Abbotsford?

Pet rules vary by complex: many allow one dog (often with a 14-to-18-inch shoulder height or 25-to-40 lb weight limit) or one cat, while a few older complexes are pet-free. Always verify the current registered pet bylaw before writing an offer.
Why do 55+ townhomes often cost less per square foot than all-ages townhomes?

Because occupancy is restricted to residents aged 55 and older, the buyer pool is narrower than unrestricted family townhomes, allowing downsizers to buy significantly more square footage and wider single-level layouts per dollar.
